posts.caption:
**Refusing to play a helpless space princess, she grabbed a blaster and became cinema's ultimate galactic rebel.**

Born October 21, 1956, in Burbank, California, today Carrie Frances Fisher would have celebrated her **70th** milestone.

The daughter of pop singer Eddie Fisher and screen legend Debbie Reynolds, Carrie grew up under relentless media scrutiny, hiding in books before making her film debut at nineteen in *Shampoo*.

In 1977, George Lucas cast her as Princess Leia in *Star Wars*. Instead of a passive damsel, Carrie brought biting wit, royal dignity, and fierce defiance, turning cinnamon buns into the eternal symbol of galactic rebellion across four decades.

Behind the silver screen, Carrie waged a courageous, public battle against bipolar disorder and addiction, transforming her pain into bestselling literary triumphs like *Postcards from the Edge* and becoming Hollywood's secret top script doctor.

Remembered for her razor-sharp honesty, glittering humor, and beloved service French bulldog Gary, Carrie Fisher proved that real royalty speaks raw truth.

**What was Carrie Fisher's finest moment: defying Darth Vader on the Death Star or her witty memoir Postcards from the Edge? Tell us below! 👇**
posts.comment:
**The secret behind Carrie Fisher's Star Wars script doctoring...**

* Carrie was Hollywood's most in-demand script doctor for over fifteen years, quietly polishing and rewriting iconic dialogue for *Sister Act*, *Hook*, *The Wedding Singer*, and the *Star Wars* prequels.
* George Lucas famously banned her from wearing a bra under her white gown in *Star Wars*, claiming there was 'no underwear in space.'

Which of these facts surprised you the most?
posts.reel_script: Born into Hollywood royalty, Carrie Fisher refused to play a helpless maiden. Grabbing a laser blaster in Star Wars, she created the ultimate symbol of female rebellion as Princess Leia, before becoming one of Hollywood's most brilliant, uncredited script doctors and bestselling authors. Remembering our eternal galactic princess on her seventieth birthday. What was your favorite scene of hers? Tell us below.

posts.caption:
**Devastated after losing the lead in Top Gun, Tom Cruise mentored him into cinema's most bankable new leading man.**

Born October 21, 1988, in Austin, Texas, today Glen Thomas Powell Jr. turns **38**, standing as modern cinema's charismatic savior.

A former high school athlete, Glen spent fifteen years enduring hundreds of humiliating auditions and uncredited bit parts in Los Angeles, couch-surfing while trying to break through.

When he lost the co-starring role of Rooster to Miles Teller for *Top Gun: Maverick*, Glen was heartbroken, but producer Tom Cruise took him aside and challenged him to turn rival pilot Hangman into an unforgettable swaggering hero.

Glen stole the skies in *Top Gun: Maverick*, before single-handedly reviving the theatrical romantic comedy with Sydney Sweeney in *Anyone But You*, writing and starring in Richard Linklater's *Hit Man*, and taming tornadoes in *Twisters*.

At 38, Glen Powell has brought back the golden era of charismatic, crowd-pleasing Hollywood movie stardom on sheer hustle and southern charm.

**Which Glen Powell blockbuster was your favorite: Hangman in Top Gun, Ben in Anyone But You, or Tyler in Twisters? Vote below! 👇**
posts.comment:
**The secret behind Tom Cruise's mentorship of Glen Powell...**

* After Glen agreed to play Hangman in *Top Gun: Maverick*, Tom Cruise paid for Glen's real-world pilot flight lessons so he could earn his pilot's license alongside him.
* Glen co-wrote his breakout hit *Hit Man* alongside director Richard Linklater after reading a 2001 Texas Monthly magazine article.

Which of these facts surprised you the most?
posts.reel_script: After losing the co-starring role in Top Gun: Maverick, Glen Powell almost walked away empty-handed. But Tom Cruise saw his star power and convinced him to play Hangman. Glen ran with it, reviving the romantic comedy in Anyone But You and conquering the box office in Twisters. Happy thirty-eighth birthday to Hollywood's hottest leading man. What is your favorite Glen Powell movie?

posts.caption:
**Surviving life-threatening leukemia twice, he learned English in months and earned an Academy Award nomination.**

Born October 21, 1959, in Koide, Niigata, Japan, today Ken Watanabe turns **67**, revered as an international titan of commanding presence.

The son of two schoolteachers, Ken trained in Tokyo classical theater, rising to become Japan's premier samurai star before being diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia in 1989, battling through chemotherapy relapses to return to the stage.

In 2003, director Edward Zwick cast him as Lord Katsumoto opposite Tom Cruise in *The Last Samurai*. Despite knowing very little English, Ken delivered a mesmerizing performance of quiet nobility that earned him an Oscar nomination for Best Supporting Actor.

He became Christopher Nolan's trusted collaborator in *Batman Begins* and *Inception*, starred in *Memoirs of a Geisha*, anchored the *Godzilla* franchise, and dominated television as detective Hiroto Katagiri in *Tokyo Vice*.

At 67, Ken Watanabe embodies dignity, survival, and profound cross-cultural mastery across world cinema.

**What is Ken Watanabe's greatest screen performance: Katsumoto in The Last Samurai, Saito in Inception, or Tokyo Vice? Share below! 👇**
posts.comment:
**The secret behind Ken Watanabe's Last Samurai casting...**

* Ken had never acted in an English-language production when cast in *The Last Samurai*; he worked with vocal coaches for up to eight hours a day to master the script's rhythm.
* In 2015, he made Broadway history as the first Japanese actor nominated for the Tony Award for Best Actor in a Musical for *The King and I*.

Which of these facts surprised you the most?
posts.reel_script: Battling through life-threatening leukemia twice, Ken Watanabe turned near-fatal adversity into legendary strength. He learned English in months to star alongside Tom Cruise in The Last Samurai, earning an Academy Award nomination before mesmerizing the world in Inception and Tokyo Vice. Happy sixty-seventh birthday to an international cinema giant. What is your favorite movie starring Ken Watanabe? Tell us in the comments.
